It differs from [Blinn-Phong Shading Model](2239-blinn-phong-shading-model.md) by using the reflected light vector for specular calculation rather than the halfway vector, and from [Phong Shading Model for Volume Data](1353-phong-shading-model-for-volume-data.md) by typically relying on pre-computed reflectance maps or explicit vector math rather than specialized volume-specific modulation tables [S3, S4].

The claim states that the model in S3 differs from Blinn-Phong by using the reflected light vector for specular calculation rather than the halfway vector. Source S3 explicitly states that the specular illumination value Is is looked up in a reflectance map indexed by the 'unnormalized reflection vector computed from the gradient and the eye vector'. Source S4 (Phong Shading Model for Volume Data) explicitly defines the specular term using the 'halfway vector h' (max(n · h, 0)). Thus, the first part of the claim is supported. The claim also states that S3 differs from S4 by relying on pre-computed reflectance maps rather than specialized volume-specific modulation tables. Source S3 describes using 'reflectance map' tables indexed by vectors. Source S4 describes a standard Phong model using explicit vector math (dot products of normal, light, and eye vectors) without mentioning pre-computed reflectance maps. Thus, the second part of the claim is supported.
